title: When the Cipher Falls
premise: Ansel Zhou, the coroner of a fading mill town, has spent years quietly correcting the record on deaths the police mislabeled, until a nervous stranger pays her to prove that a murder has not yet happened. The supposed victim is Marisol Vega, a witness set to testify against a shipping magnate, and every official document insists she died two years ago. As Ansel digs, she realizes the town's beloved sheriff helped fake the death to protect Marisol — and that someone inside the conspiracy is now hunting the living woman for real. Ansel must choose between exposing a justice system that lied for good reasons and letting an innocent die; in the end she fakes Marisol's second death so convincingly that even the law believes it, smuggling her out of town while Ansel finally accepts that belonging means being seen, not hidden.
about_author: Hazel Eastwick is the pen name of a former rural paramedic who spent a decade writing case notes no one read and stories everyone did. She lives near the coast with two indifferent cats and a growing collection of unsolved crossword puzzles.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Deaths
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. We meet her at a graveside funeral, cataloguing the town's dead by memory, then in her office where she keeps a private ledger of three 'accidents' she quietly proved were murders. The beat: competent loneliness — a woman who prefers the company of the dead because they don't ask questions.

chapters.title: A Deposit Against Nothing
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A gaunt stranger named Corrigan leaves an envelope of cash: prove that Marisol Vega will not be murdered. Ansel checks records and finds Marisol legally dead since two years ago. The beat: unease — the first client whose request makes less sense the more she examines it.

chapters.title: Everyone Swears She's Dead
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, with a flashback interlude from Marisol. Ansel interviews the sheriff, the priest, and Marisol's sister, all of whom grieve convincingly — too convincingly. The beat: creeping suspicion as grief starts looking rehearsed.

chapters.title: What the Water Kept
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Dredging the old quarry where Marisol supposedly drowned, Ansel finds the coffin empty except for weighted sandbags stamped with the shipping company's mark. The beat: cold clarity — the lie was institutional, not personal.

chapters.title: The Sheriff's Good Lie
chapters.summary: Sheriff Dale Okafor's POV. He confesses he helped stage Marisol's death to shield her from Hargrove's men before trial, believing it the only justice available. The beat: sympathy for the devil — duty and decency pulling in opposite directions.

chapters.title: Corrigan's Second Envelope
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Corrigan returns demanding proof on a deadline; Ansel realizes he isn't protecting Marisol but confirming the kill order for Hargrove. Her office is searched, her ledger photographed. The beat: fear — invisibility was always a fragile shelter.

chapters.title: Alive at the End of Route 9
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Ansel traces Marisol to a shuttered roadside motel; their first meeting is wary, almost hostile — Marisol resents being found. But Ansel shows her the sandbags and the new kill contract. The beat: reluctant alliance between two women who both survive by disappearing.

chapters.title: Ninety-Six Hours
chapters.summary: Alternating Ansel and Marisol POVs. They build a counter-fake: documents, dental records, a body from the county morgue, a staged accident timed to Corrigan's deadline. The sheriff must choose again — this time he helps. The beat: taut momentum, trust assembled under pressure.

chapters.title: The Second Funeral
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The trap springs: Corrigan reports the 'successful' hit, Hargrove's fixers are recorded confessing, and the evidence goes to a state investigator Ansel once helped. Corrigan, cornered, nearly kills Marisol before the sheriff intervenes. The beat: climax — violence, sacrifice, and the ledger finally opened in daylight.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, closing with Marisol's letter from afar. Hargrove falls; the sheriff resigns but stays in town; Ansel testifies, publicly, for the first time. Marisol sends word she's safe and alive under a new name. The beat: resolution — Ansel stops hiding, and the town finally sees her.
